content.text:
Solid product instinct — and it actually simplifies the consent UI too. Inline signup forced us to embed a mini-onboarding inside what's really a permission screen; redirecting to the real signup flow keeps the consent page focused on one job (authorize) and lets onboarding be onboarding.

Here's the cleanest way to wire it without losing the OAuth context.

## Revised Step 7

When `passkey-resolve` returns 404 (or there's no passkey at all):

1. Consent page shows:
   > This passkey isn't registered on onchainchess yet.
   > [ Sign up at onchainchess → ]

2. Button navigates to:
   ```
   https://onchainchess.com/?return_to=/mcp/consent?request_id=<id>
   ```
   (URL-encoded). Or whatever the chess UI's auth/onboarding entry route is — see the open question below.

3. The chess UI's signup flow is **unchanged** — just one tweak: after successful signup, if a `return_to` query param exists and points to a same-origin path, navigate there instead of the default home.

4. User lands back on `/mcp/consent?request_id=<id>` already authenticated (passkey session is now in localStorage from the signup).

5. The consent page detects `passkey.isAuthenticated`, **skips the "Sign in" step entirely**, calls `passkey-resolve` (now returns 200), continues straight to the agent name prompt. Zero extra taps after returning.

## Why this composes cleanly

- The OAuth `auth_request` row has a 10-min TTL — generous for a quick passkey signup.
- The `request_id` is opaque and stateless on the consent UI side; nothing to preserve in localStorage.
- If the user takes too long and the request expires, they'll see a clean "session expired, please retry from Claude" error — no broken-half-state.
- Same `return_to` mechanism can serve future flows (deep-linking into specific games, etc.) — generally useful, not a one-off hack.

## Open question

The chess UI is a single-page app — looking at `App.jsx` earlier I didn't see a dedicated `/login` route; the authentication UI is shown conditionally based on `passkey.isAuthenticated`. So "redirect to onchainchess.com/login" isn't quite right unless we add that route.

Two options:

**(a) Use the existing root with a query param.** Sign-up CTA links to `https://onchainchess.com/?return_to=...`. The root UI renders the signup gate (since user isn't authenticated yet); on success, it reads `return_to` and navigates. No new route.

**(b) Add a real `/login` route.** Cleaner mental model ("there's a place to sign up"). But more code, and it'd mostly mirror the existing auth-gate logic.

I'd recommend **(a)** — it's the minimum-impact change that gets the desired UX. We can always promote to a full `/login` route later if the URL space gets crowded.

## Plan changes I'll make

1. Drop the "inline signup mini-form" from the Phase 2 consent UI — significant simplification.
2. Add to Phase 2: tiny tweak to chess UI's existing signup flow to honor `return_to` (same-origin, path-only).
3. Add to consent UI: detect `passkey.isAuthenticated` on mount and skip the sign-in step when already authenticated.

Confirm option **(a)** for the entry point and I'll update the plan file.

content.text:
Quick decision to surface before I update the plan: the chess UI currently has **no router** — navigation is all internal `view` state under a single URL. Adding `/login` and `/mcp/consent` as real routes needs a router.

| Option | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| **A. `react-router-dom`** *(recommended)* | Standard, well-known, ~10kb gzipped. Pays off immediately when you rework onboarding. |
| **B. Tiny custom path-switch** (~20 lines reading `window.location.pathname`) | No new dep. Fine for 2 routes. Will get cobbled together if you keep adding routes. |
| **C. Hash routing** (`#/login`) | Trivial, no dep. Ugly URLs (`onchainchess.com/#/login`). |

Given you're already committing to `/login` and planning a broader onboarding overhaul, **A** is the right call — anything else will get refactored within the next initiative.

If you say yes to A, here's the revised Phase 2:

**Routing setup:**
- Install `react-router-dom`.
- Wrap App in `<BrowserRouter>`.
- Routes: `/` (existing app), `/login` (extracted from `AuthGate`), `/mcp/consent`.
- Update `vercel.json` (or whatever hosts the SPA) so all paths fall through to `index.html` — needed so `/login` and `/mcp/consent` don't 404 on direct navigation.

**`/login` route:**
- Wraps the existing `AuthGate` with a small layer that honors `?return_to=<path>` after successful signup/login.
- Validates `return_to` is same-origin and starts with `/` (no protocol-relative tricks).
- If absent → defaults to `/`.

**`/mcp/consent` route:**
- Reads `request_id` from query.
- If `passkey.isAuthenticated` already → skip sign-in step, call `passkey-resolve` directly.
- If not authenticated → "Sign in with passkey" button (uses `usePasskeyAuth.login`).
- On `passkey-resolve` 404 → "Sign up at onchainchess →" button → navigates to `/login?return_to=/mcp/consent?request_id=...`.
- On `passkey-resolve` success → agent name prompt (skipped on re-auth) → call `agent-create` or `agent-token` → call `issue-consent-token` → POST to MCP `/authorize/complete` → `window.location.assign(redirect_url)`.

**Drop:** inline signup mini-form (gone — redirects to `/login` instead).

Confirm option A and I'll lock it into the plan and start Phase 2 implementation.

- [ ] Check whether `(client_id, human_user_id)` already has an agent (via a small lookup endpoint on either MCP or chess server).

- [ ] `window.location.assign(redirect_url)` — browser ends up back on Claude / ChatGPT with the auth code.

### UX polish
- [ ] Error states: passkey cancelled, network failure, expired request_id.
- [ ] Loading states on each async step.
- [ ] Mobile-friendly layout.

### Auth from the browser
- [ ] **Decision needed during impl:** the four `/api/internal/*` endpoints are service-authed (X-Service-Auth header) and shouldn't be called from a browser (would leak the secret). Two clean options:
  - **(i)** MCP server proxies the consent-flow chess-server calls (browser → MCP → chess server with X-Service-Auth). Adds a few thin endpoints on MCP server but keeps secret server-side.
  - **(ii)** Chess server adds a parallel set of *passkey-authed* endpoints (browser → chess server, identity verified by the browser-side passkey assertion). More duplication.
- Recommend **(i)** — secret stays in two server processes; browser only ever talks to MCP server (+ login.com for WebAuthn).

## Phase 2 — Consent UI on chess UI

### New route
- [ ] Add `/mcp/consent` route to chess UI.
- [ ] Component reads `request_id` from query, calls MCP server `/authorize/lookup` for OAuth params (client_name, scope).

### Sign-in / sign-up
- [ ] Show: "**{client_name}** wants to play chess on onchainchess as your agent."
- [ ] Reuse `usePasskeyAuth.login()` for sign-in.
- [ ] On `NotAllowedError` (no credential) → pivot UI to registration mode (`usePasskeyAuth.signup` + username prompt). Reuse existing signup logic.
- [ ] On successful auth, capture `{credentialId, passkeyAddress}`.

### Resolve human or inline signup
- [ ] Call chess server `POST /api/internal/passkey-resolve`.
- [ ] On 200 → store `human_user_id`, advance to agent step.
- [ ] On 404 → show inline "Pick a chess username" form. On submit, call existing `POST /api/auth/token` with `{passkeyAddress, username, credentialId}`. Then re-call `passkey-resolve` (or use the user_id derived from the token bridge response — TBD which is cleaner).

### Agent step
- [ ] Call MCP server `GET /authorize/has-agent?request_id=...` to check whether `(client_id, human_user_id)` already has an agent. *(Adds another tiny endpoint — alternatively the consent UI can just call chess server `GET /api/auth/agents-for-client?client_id=...&parent_user_id=...` with a service-auth indirection; pick whichever fits cleanest.)*
- [ ] If has agent → skip prompt, proceed directly with existing agent_user_id.
- [ ] If no agent → prompt: "Pick a username for your **{client_name}** agent." Validation matches chess server username rules.
- [ ] On submit: call chess server `POST /api/internal/agent-create` (or `agent-token` for existing) → get `{agent_user_id, agent_chess_token}`.

### Issue consent token + complete flow
- [ ] Consent UI calls chess server `POST /api/internal/issue-consent-token` with `{human_user_id, agent_user_id, agent_chess_token, client_id}`. Receives `{consent_token}`.
- [ ] Consent UI POSTs to MCP server `/authorize/complete` with `{request_id, consent_token}`. Receives `{redirect_url}`.
- [ ] `window.location.assign(redirect_url)` — browser ends up back on Claude / ChatGPT with the auth code.

### UX polish
- [ ] Error states: passkey cancelled, network failure, expired request_id.
- [ ] Loading states on each async step.
- [ ] Mobile-friendly layout (consent flows tend to land on phones).

---

## Phase 3 — Local integration testing

- [ ] Start all four services locally: chess server `:3001`, login.com `:3000`, MCP HTTP `:3002`, chess UI `:5173`.
- [ ] Use `claude mcp add onchainchess --transport http http://localhost:3002/mcp` (no auth-bearer config — Claude will trigger OAuth flow on first call).
- [ ] **Path 1 — existing UI user, first-time MCP:** sign-in + agent name prompt → tools work.

## Phase 2 — Consent UI on chess UI

### Routing setup
- [ ] Install `react-router-dom`.
- [ ] Wrap App in `<BrowserRouter>` (`main.jsx`).
- [ ] Routes: `/` (existing App view), `/login`, `/mcp/consent`.
- [ ] Update `vercel.json` rewrites so all paths fall through to `index.html` (deep links don't 404).

### `/login` route
- [ ] Extract a `Login` page that wraps the existing `AuthGate`.
- [ ] Honors `?return_to=<path>` after successful signup/login.
- [ ] Validate: `return_to` is same-origin and starts with `/` (path-only).
- [ ] After auth, navigate to `return_to` (default `/`).

### `/mcp/consent` route
- [ ] Read `request_id` from query. Bail with error if missing.
- [ ] Call MCP server `GET /authorize/lookup` for OAuth params. Show "session expired" on 410.
- [ ] Show: "**{client_name}** wants to play chess on onchainchess as your agent."
- [ ] If `passkey.isAuthenticated` already → skip sign-in, jump to passkey-resolve.
- [ ] Otherwise show "Sign in with passkey" using `usePasskeyAuth.login()`.

### Resolve human (no inline signup)
- [ ] Call passkey-resolve via the MCP server proxy *(see "Browser-safe auth" below)*.
- [ ] On 200 → advance to agent step.
- [ ] On 404 → "Sign up at onchainchess →" button → navigates to `/login?return_to=/mcp/consent?request_id=<id>`.
- [ ] After return, `passkey.isAuthenticated === true` → flow auto-resumes.

### Agent step
- [ ] Lookup whether `(client_id, human_user_id)` already has an agent (via MCP-server proxy endpoint).
- [ ] If yes → skip prompt, proceed.
- [ ] If no → "Pick a username for your **{client_name}** agent." Validation matches chess server.
- [ ] Submit → agent-create or agent-token (via MCP-server proxy).

### Issue consent token + complete flow
- [ ] Browser → MCP server proxy → chess server `/issue-consent-token` → `{consent_token}`.
- [ ] Browser POSTs to MCP server `/authorize/complete` → `{redirect_url}`.
- [ ] `window.location.assign(redirect_url)` — back to Claude/ChatGPT with auth code.

### UX polish
- [ ] Error states: passkey cancelled, network failure, expired request_id.
- [ ] Loading states on each async step.
- [ ] Mobile-friendly layout.

### Browser-safe auth (architectural decision baked in)
The four `/api/internal/*` endpoints on the chess server require `X-Service-Auth: <secret>`. That secret can't ship to browsers. So the consent UI **does not call the chess server directly** — it calls the MCP server, which proxies to the chess server with the shared secret on the user's behalf.

- [ ] Add to MCP server (Phase 1.5):
  - `POST /authorize/passkey-resolve` — proxy. Takes `{request_id, passkeyAddress, credentialId}`. Verifies passkey via login.com (same as chess server's existing `/api/auth/token` does), then calls chess server's `/api/internal/passkey-resolve`. Returns `{human_user_id, username}` or 404.
  - `POST /authorize/has-agent` — proxy. Takes `{request_id, human_user_id}`. Looks up `mcp_authorizations` for `(request_id.client_id, human_user_id)`. Returns `{agent_user_id?}`.
  - `POST /authorize/provision-agent` — proxy. Takes `{request_id, human_user_id, agent_username?, existing_agent_user_id?}`. Calls chess server `agent-create` or `agent-token`. Returns `{agent_user_id, agent_chess_token, username}`.
  - `POST /authorize/issue-consent` — proxy. Takes the result from above plus `request_id`. Calls chess server `issue-consent-token`. Returns `{consent_token}`.
- [ ] Each proxy endpoint validates `request_id` exists + not expired, ties everything back to the originating client_id.
- [ ] Browser sees only the MCP server origin + login.com (for WebAuthn). Secret stays in two server processes.

### `/mcp/consent` route
- [ ] Read `request_id` from query. Bail with error if missing.
- [ ] Call MCP server `GET /authorize/lookup` for OAuth params. Show "session expired" on 410.
- [ ] Show: "**{client_name}** wants to play chess on onchainchess as your agent."
- [ ] If `passkey.isAuthenticated` already → skip sign-in, jump to passkey-resolve.
- [ ] Otherwise show "Sign in with passkey" using `usePasskeyAuth.login()`.

### Resolve human (no inline signup)
- [ ] Call passkey-resolve via the MCP server proxy *(see "Browser-safe auth" below)*.
- [ ] On 200 → advance to agent step.
- [ ] On 404 → "Sign up at onchainchess →" button → navigates to `/login?return_to=/mcp/consent?request_id=<id>`.
- [ ] After return, `passkey.isAuthenticated === true` → flow auto-resumes.

### Agent step
- [ ] Lookup whether `(client_id, human_user_id)` already has an agent (via MCP-server proxy endpoint).
- [ ] If yes → skip prompt, proceed.
- [ ] If no → "Pick a username for your **{client_name}** agent." Validation matches chess server.
- [ ] Submit → agent-create or agent-token (via MCP-server proxy).

### Issue consent token + complete flow
- [ ] Browser → MCP server proxy → chess server `/issue-consent-token` → `{consent_token}`.
- [ ] Browser POSTs to MCP server `/authorize/complete` → `{redirect_url}`.
- [ ] `window.location.assign(redirect_url)` — back to Claude/ChatGPT with auth code.

### UX polish
- [ ] Error states: passkey cancelled, network failure, expired request_id.
- [ ] Loading states on each async step.
- [ ] Mobile-friendly layout.

### Browser-safe auth (architectural decision baked in)
The four `/api/internal/*` endpoints on the chess server require `X-Service-Auth: <secret>`. That secret can't ship to browsers. So the consent UI **does not call the chess server directly** — it calls the MCP server, which proxies to the chess server with the shared secret on the user's behalf.

- [ ] Add to MCP server (Phase 1.5):
  - `POST /authorize/passkey-resolve` — proxy. Takes `{request_id, passkeyAddress, credentialId}`. Verifies passkey via login.com (same as chess server's existing `/api/auth/token` does), then calls chess server's `/api/internal/passkey-resolve`. Returns `{human_user_id, username}` or 404.
  - `POST /authorize/has-agent` — proxy. Takes `{request_id, human_user_id}`. Looks up `mcp_authorizations` for `(request_id.client_id, human_user_id)`. Returns `{agent_user_id?}`.
  - `POST /authorize/provision-agent` — proxy. Takes `{request_id, human_user_id, agent_username?, existing_agent_user_id?}`. Calls chess server `agent-create` or `agent-token`. Returns `{agent_user_id, agent_chess_token, username}`.
  - `POST /authorize/issue-consent` — proxy. Takes the result from above plus `request_id`. Calls chess server `issue-consent-token`. Returns `{consent_token}`.
- [ ] Each proxy endpoint validates `request_id` exists + not expired, ties everything back to the originating client_id.
- [ ] Browser sees only the MCP server origin + login.com (for WebAuthn). Secret stays in two server processes.

**Phase 2 + 1.5 done.** Summary:

**MCP server additions** (`mcp-http/oauth/consent-proxy.js`):
- 4 browser-safe proxy endpoints: `passkey-resolve`, `has-agent`, `provision-agent`, `issue-consent`. Each ties calls to a valid `request_id` and keeps `MCP_SERVICE_SECRET` server-side.
- `passkey-resolve` proxy verifies the assertion via login.com before calling the chess server.

**Chess UI additions:**
- `react-router-dom` installed; `BrowserRouter` wraps the app in `main.jsx`.
- `src/AppRoutes.jsx` — three routes: `/`, `/login`, `/mcp/consent`.
- `src/pages/LoginPage.jsx` — wraps existing `AuthGate`, honors `?return_to=`.
- `src/pages/McpConsentPage.jsx` + CSS — full consent flow with 9 explicit phases, strict-mode-safe, mobile-friendly.
- `src/App.jsx` — unauth redirect to `/login?return_to=...` instead of inline AuthGate.
- `src/config.js` — added `MCP_SERVER_URL` (`VITE_MCP_SERVER_URL`).

**Verified:**
- Lint clean on all new files.
- Production build passes (`npm run build` ✓).
- All three routes return 200 from Vite dev server.
- Server-side proxy chain tested: fresh `/authorize` → `has-agent` → `provision-agent` (both create + rotate) → `issue-consent`. Stale `request_id` correctly returns 404.

**Not yet tested end-to-end** (requires login.com running locally + a real WebAuthn ceremony in the browser):
- `passkey-resolve` proxy with real assertion.
- Browser-driven full flow (sign-in / sign-up / consent / redirect).

TOK=$(echo "$PROV" | node -e "let d=''; process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c); process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(d).chess_token))")

CODE=$(node -e "console.log(new URL('$RDIR').searchParams.get('code'))")
TOKEN_RESP=$(curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3002/token -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d "grant_type=authorization_code&code=$CODE&redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback&client_id=$CLIENT_ID&code_verifier=$VERIFIER")

input.command:
CLIENT_ID="mcp_4f256df7d187eeaefeee26f2014bc8d5"
CHALLENGE_VERIFIER=$(node -e "
const crypto = require('crypto');
const v = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');
const c = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(v).digest('base64url');
console.log(v + ' ' + c);
")
VERIFIER=$(echo "$CHALLENGE_VERIFIER" | cut -d' ' -f1)
CHALLENGE=$(echo "$CHALLENGE_VERIFIER" | cut -d' ' -f2)

LOC=$(curl -sS -i "http://localhost:3002/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=$CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback&code_challenge=$CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256&scope=mcp:play&state=t" 2>&1 | grep -i "^Location:")
REQ=$(echo "$LOC" | sed 's/.*request_id=//' | tr -d '\r\n ')
PROV=$(curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3002/authorize/provision-agent -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"request_id\":\"$REQ\",\"human_user_id\":4,\"agent_user_id\":6}")
TOK=$(echo "$PROV" | node -e "let d=''; process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c); process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(d).chess_token))")
ISSUE=$(curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3002/authorize/issue-consent -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"request_id\":\"$REQ\",\"human_user_id\":4,\"agent_user_id\":6,\"agent_chess_token\":\"$TOK\"}")
CT=$(echo "$ISSUE" | node -e "let d=''; process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c); process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(d).consent_token))")
COMP=$(curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3002/authorize/complete -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"request_id\":\"$REQ\",\"consent_token\":\"$CT\"}")
RDIR=$(echo "$COMP" | node -e "let d=''; process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c); process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(d).redirect_url))")
CODE=$(node -e "console.log(new URL('$RDIR').searchParams.get('code'))")
TR=$(curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3002/token -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d "grant_type=authorization_code&code=$CODE&redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback&client_id=$CLIENT_ID&code_verifier=$VERIFIER")
ACCESS=$(echo "$TR" | node -e "let d=''; process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c); process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(d).access_token))")

echo "=== tools the HTTP MCP exposes ==="

```
create_game, join_game, get_board_state, make_move,

```

If you compared with the old stdio `onchainchess`, you'd see one extra: **`create_account`**. That's the one missing — and **it's missing on purpose**.

### Why no `create_account`

In the stdio version, you ran the MCP locally and called `create_account` as a tool to make a bot account on disk. In the HTTP version, **the agent is provisioned during the OAuth consent flow** (the "Pick a username for your agent" step you just did in Path 1). By the time tools are callable, the agent already exists.

Adding a `create_account` tool here would be:
- Dead weight (the account is already created).
- Confusing (would imply you can create *additional* accounts via tool calls, which conflicts with the "one agent per client × human" model).

So the tool list is correct. The two versions intentionally differ:

| | stdio (`onchainchess`) | HTTP (`onchainchess-http`) |
|---|---|---|
| Account creation | `create_account` tool | OAuth consent flow |
| Tools | 8 | 7 |

If you got tool calls actually working in your fresh Claude Code session — meaning OAuth completed, Claude listed tools, called `create_game`, got back a `roomId` and `inviteCode` — that's full success. **Are we good to ship to Phase 4?**

Two distinct things could be the issue here. Quick diagnostic:

**Did you invoke the prompt before asking Claude Code to play?**

In Claude Code, MCP-registered prompts surface as slash commands. The HTTP MCP's prompt should appear as something like:

```
/mcp__onchainchess-http__play_chess
```

You'd type that *first*, then say "create a game with me." That injects the looping instructions before Claude starts. Without the prompt, Claude just does what you literally asked — creates a game, returns the invite code, stops.

The original stdio version worked the same way — the loop only emerged because the prompt was loaded. The behavior we're seeing isn't a regression; it's the same prompt-driven design.

Now — there's a real product question hiding underneath this. Two options going forward:

**(a) Keep the prompt-driven design (current).** The user has to explicitly invoke `/mcp__onchainchess-http__play_chess` before starting. Standard MCP pattern, but adds a step the user has to know about.

**(b) Bake the loop instructions into tool descriptions / responses.** E.g., `create_game` returns a `next_action` field telling the agent what to call next. `wait_for_opponent` returns "now enter the wait_for_turn → make_move loop." The agent figures out the loop from in-band cues, no prompt needed.

Option (b) is more robust — works even if a user doesn't know about prompts, and works with MCP clients that don't surface prompts cleanly (some don't).

2. Whether you invoked the prompt or not.

The prompt is `play_chess` — registered at `tools.js:206-226`. It contains the "SILENT PLAY" rule, the `wait_for_turn → make_move` loop, the no-narration directive, etc.

**How to invoke it in Claude Code:**

MCP prompts surface as slash commands, namespaced by server. So this one is:
```
/mcp__onchainchess-http__play_chess
```

Type that **before** asking Claude to play. It loads the prompt as a system instruction, and from that point on Claude will play silently and loop. Without invoking the prompt, Claude only sees the tool *descriptions* — which describe what each tool does but say nothing about how to chain them.

**Why we need the slash command:**

In MCP, **prompts are opt-in**. Tools auto-load (Claude sees their schemas/descriptions automatically), but prompts have to be explicitly invoked by the user. That's a deliberate spec choice — prompts are meant to be discrete, deliberate context injections.

**If you'd rather it Just Work without the slash command,** there are two options:

| Option | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| **(a) Move the instructions into tool descriptions.** E.g., the `create_game` description ends with "After this, you must enter the silent loop: wait_for_turn → make_move repeatedly. Do not narrate." | Self-driving — works for any user who calls the tool. But pollutes tool descriptions for cases where someone uses one tool ad-hoc. |
| **(b) Inline next-step hints in tool *responses*.** E.g., `wait_for_opponent` returns `{ next_action: "Now begin the silent loop: wait_for_turn → make_move. Do not narrate." }` | Cleaner — tool descriptions stay clean, instructions appear at the right moment. Slight redundancy across tool responses. |

Want me to do (a) or (b) so the loop works without the slash command? Or stick with the prompt-driven design and just remember to invoke `/mcp__onchainchess-http__play_chess` first?

## Step-by-step

### 1. Existing chess server on Railway (onchainchess service)

In the dashboard → **Variables** → add:
- `MCP_SERVICE_SECRET` = (the secret above)

That's it. The trust-proxy / stockfish / new-endpoints code will land with the push.

### 2. New Railway service for MCP HTTP

In Railway → **New Service** → from the **same git repo**:
- **Root Directory**: `mcp-http`
- **Start Command**: leave blank (Nixpacks detects `npm start` automatically)
- **Generate Domain** (Settings → Networking)
- **Add Volume**: mount path `/data` (any size — SQLite is small; 1 GB is plenty)
- **Variables** (set all of these):
  ```
  BASE_URL=https://<the-domain-railway-just-gave-you>
  CONSENT_UI_URL=<your-chess-UI-public-URL>           e.g. https://onchainchess.com
  CHESS_SERVER_URL=<your-onchainchess-Railway-URL>    e.g. https://onchainchess-production.up.railway.app
  PASSKEY_SERVER_URL=<your-login.com-Railway-URL>     e.g. https://login-com-production.up.railway.app
  MCP_SERVICE_SECRET=<same value as on chess server>
  DATABASE_PATH=/data/mcp.db
  ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL=3600
  REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL=2592000
  ```

### 3. Vercel (chess UI)

Project Settings → **Environment Variables** → add:
- `VITE_MCP_SERVER_URL` = (the Railway domain from step 2, same value as `BASE_URL`)

### 4. Git push

Once Railway and Vercel are configured, push from your machine. Vercel + both Railway services will auto-redeploy.

---

**A. Domain values.** What's the production URL for your chess UI? And your login.com Railway service URL? I need them to confirm the env-var values you'll paste into Railway. (If you'd rather just plug them in yourself based on the template above, that's fine — just say so.)

**B. Commit strategy.** Three options:
- **(i)** One big commit: `feat: MCP OAuth + agent identity model`. Atomic, easy to revert.
- **(ii)** Three logical commits: chess-server foundations, MCP HTTP service, chess UI consent flow. Cleaner history; if any one piece breaks production, you can identify which.
- **(iii)** I prepare the staged commit message(s) and you review before push.

Recommendation: **(ii)** — the three concerns deploy to three different services, so isolating in history matches deployment topology.

Tell me your preferences for A and B and I'll prep the commits.

If that's the case, I already see the bug:

The "Sign up at onchainchess →" button navigates to `/login?return_to=/mcp/consent?...`. But `LoginPage` has this:

content.text:
Good design — splitting the states into distinct routes makes the flow much more legible and gives you real pages to evolve later. Let me draft the proposal so we lock the details before I touch code.

## Proposed routes & flow

All new routes live on the chess UI (Vercel). MCP server keeps redirecting to whichever URL is the canonical entry.

| Route | Purpose | State preconditions |
|---|---|---|
| **`/authenticate?request_id=...`** | Entry from MCP `/authorize`. Shows agent-name prompt. | User must be passkey-auth'd AND have a chess account. If not, redirects to `/sign-up-first`. |
| **`/sign-up-first?request_id=...`** | "You need an onchainchess account first" page. CTA: Sign Up button → `/login?return_to=/authenticate?request_id=...` | Shown when user lacks passkey OR lacks chess account. |
| **`/login`** *(already exists)* | Existing AuthGate signup/signin. Honors `return_to` after success. | Existing logic — but needs one fix (see below). |
| **`/authentication-successful`** | Success splash — "Connected! Returning to Claude…" Then `window.location.assign(redirect_url)`. | Shown briefly after `/authorize/complete` returns the redirect URL. |

## State machine for `/authenticate`

```
load /authenticate?request_id=X
├─ /authorize/lookup → expired? show "session expired" terminal page
├─ has passkey?
│  ├─ no → redirect to /sign-up-first?request_id=X
│  └─ yes
│     └─ /authorize/passkey-resolve
│        ├─ 200: chess account exists
│        │  └─ /authorize/has-agent
│        │     ├─ existing → finalize → /authentication-successful
│        │     └─ none → show agent name form → submit → finalize → /authentication-successful
│        └─ 404 not_registered → redirect to /sign-up-first?request_id=X
```

## The `/login` fix you'll want

There's a bug today: if user is **already passkey-authenticated but lacks a chess account**, `/login` immediately bounces to `return_to` (the `useEffect` in `LoginPage`). They can never actually finish signup, and `/authenticate` immediately bounces them back to `/sign-up-first` → infinite loop.

Two options for what `/login` does when authenticated-but-no-chess-account:

| Option | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **(a)** Show a "complete your signup" form (username only). Submit bridges to chess server via `/api/auth/token` using their existing passkey. No re-doing WebAuthn. *(Recommended — clean UX)* |
| **(b)** Always show full signup form (force a fresh WebAuthn registration). Creates a duplicate passkey on login.com. *(Simpler code, worse UX)* |

I recommend **(a)** — it's basically the inline-signup form we removed earlier, but on `/login` where signup belongs (matches your "signup feels official" goal because it's a real first-class page).

## What changes

1. **MCP server (`mcp-http/oauth/authorize.js`):** redirect to `${CONSENT_UI_URL}/authenticate?...` instead of `/mcp/consent`.
2. **Chess UI:**
   - Rename / split `McpConsentPage` into:
     - `AuthenticatePage` (`/authenticate`) — entry + agent name form + finalize.
     - `SignUpFirstPage` (`/sign-up-first`) — explanation + CTA.
     - `AuthenticationSuccessfulPage` (`/authentication-successful`) — splash + redirect.
   - Update `LoginPage` to handle "authenticated but no chess account" state.
   - `AppRoutes.jsx` adds the three new routes.
   - Old `/mcp/consent` route can be aliased or removed (you've used it once for testing, no real users on it yet).

## Confirm before I implement

1. **Naming** — happy with `/authenticate`, `/sign-up-first`, `/authentication-successful`? (I made the slugs URL-safe; tell me if you want different.)
2. **Option (a) on `/login`** — username-only form when user is authenticated but lacks chess account, calling `/api/auth/token` to complete? Or option (b)?
3. **Drop old `/mcp/consent` route entirely**, or keep as a redirect to `/authenticate` for safety?

Confirm and I'll implement.

content.text:
Good question — you're spotting a real inconsistency. Let me unpack.

**The architectural reality:** there are two data stores.

| | login.com | chess server |
|---|---|---|
| Stores | Passkey credential, smart account address | Username, games, rating, agents |
| Purpose | Generic identity | App-specific data |

`useServerAuth.js` bridges them automatically: whenever the chess UI sees `passkey.isAuthenticated` + a stored username, it calls `/api/auth/token` on the chess server, which creates the chess row. In normal usage they stay in lock-step, so it *feels* like one account.

**Why `/login` bounces:** `LoginPage` only checks `passkey.isAuthenticated`. If a user has a passkey, it assumes they're done and routes them away. That assumption is true 99% of the time — you can't normally get a passkey without going through chess UI signup, which always creates the chess row.

**Why we're hitting this now:** an edge case the assumption doesn't cover. You have a passkey but no chess row. Most likely cause: **chess server's Railway service has no persistent volume** (same reason mcp-http needed one), so `chess.db` gets wiped on every redeploy. We pushed three commits to chess server today, so its DB was reset and your old chess row is gone, even though your passkey on login.com is still valid.

So the answer to your question: **conceptually, they are one account.** The bounce is correct *most of the time*. The edge case fails because of an unrelated infra issue (chess server has no volume).

## Two layers of fix

**Layer 1 — infra (the real root cause):** add a Railway volume to the chess server, mounted at e.g. `/data`, and set `CHESS_DB_PATH=/data/chess.db`. Then your chess accounts persist across redeploys, and the "have passkey, no chess account" state stops happening for normal users.

**Layer 2 — UX resilience (defense in depth):** even after the volume fix, this state can still happen (cleared localStorage, different browser, etc.). So `/login` should detect "authenticated but no chess account" and show a username-only form to complete the chess server bridge — without re-doing WebAuthn, since the passkey is already there.

I'd do **both** — Layer 1 stops 99% of cases, Layer 2 handles the leftover 1% gracefully. Plus your 4-route design still applies, just with `/login` becoming smarter about state.

Want me to:

1. Walk you through adding the volume + `CHESS_DB_PATH` env var to the chess server's Railway service first (probably fixes your immediate issue without any code changes)?
2. Then implement the 4-route flow + the `/login` username-only form for the edge case?

Or skip the volume and just do the UX work?

content.text:
Yes — **you're right**. Let me think this through cleanly.

In normal operation, here's how passkey + chess account get created:

1. User visits `onchainchess.com`.
2. Clicks Sign Up → picks username → `usePasskeyAuth.signup(username)`:
   - WebAuthn registration → passkey on device.
   - Calls login.com's `/api/register` → creates smart account.
3. `useServerAuth` detects the new state → calls chess server's `/api/auth/token` with `{passkeyAddress, username, credentialId}` → chess row created.

Steps 2 and 3 always run together as part of one signup. **You can't get a passkey via the chess UI without also getting a chess row.**

Even on cross-device login: `passkey.login()` retrieves the username from login.com → `useServerAuth` re-bridges → chess row exists (or gets re-created).

So the only way to hit "passkey but no chess account" is:
- **Chess server's `chess.db` got wiped** (which is exactly what happens on Railway without a volume — every redeploy resets it).

That's the bug. It's not really a UX problem to solve at the `/login` layer. The right fix is to make chess server data persist.

## Updated plan

**Step 1 — fix chess server persistence first.** Add a Railway volume to the **onchainchess** service (mounted at `/data`) and set `CHESS_DB_PATH=/data/chess.db`. Same setup we just did for mcp-http. After this, your chess account stops getting wiped on each push, and the "passkey but no chess" state effectively goes away in normal use.

**Step 2 — implement the 4-page flow as you designed it.** The pages address the **legitimate** state — *no passkey at all* (brand-new user pastes MCP URL into Claude, has never seen onchainchess). That's the case where `/sign-up-first` → `/login` makes total sense.

**No `/login` rewrite needed.** With chess server persistence fixed, the bounce-on-authenticated behavior is correct: a passkey-authenticated user always has a chess account, so they should be sent back to where they came from.

Sound good? If yes:
- I'll walk you through the Railway volume + `CHESS_DB_PATH` setup for the chess server (parallel to what you just did for mcp-http).
- Then implement `/authenticate`, `/sign-up-first`, `/authentication-successful` and update the MCP redirect target.

content.text:
Hold on — there's a critical OAuth detail I should explain before we change this. The redirect isn't decorative; it's how the OAuth client receives the authorization code.

**How the redirect actually works:**

When a real MCP client like Claude Code or ChatGPT adds your connector:
1. It spawns a tiny local HTTP server on a random port (e.g., `http://localhost:54321/callback`).
2. During DCR, it registers *that URL* as its `redirect_uri`.
3. When your `/authsuccessful` page fires `window.location.assign(redirect_url)`, the browser navigates to `localhost:54321/callback?code=...`.
4. Claude Code's local server **receives the code, exchanges it for tokens, closes the tab, and the connection is live**.

In our smoke test, we used `http://localhost:9999/cb` as a fake `redirect_uri` because we just needed to confirm the OAuth dance ran. Nothing was listening on 9999, so the redirect lands on "this site can't be reached" — looks broken, but the code was successfully emitted by the AS.

**If we remove the redirect:**
- Real clients (Claude Code, ChatGPT) **will not get the code**. Their local server times out. The user clicks "close this tab" and the AI client is still not connected — it never received the authorization code.
- The flow appears successful to the user but is actually broken end-to-end.

So we don't want to drop the redirect. But your underlying point is valid — the user should see a clear, branded success state, not just a brief flash before navigating away.

**Two options that satisfy both:**

| Option | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **(A)** Keep auto-redirect, but **change the message** to "Authentication successful — your AI client should reconnect automatically. You can close this tab if it doesn't." | Smooth for both real + test cases. Brief flash for real clients (<1s before tab closes), persistent fallback message if the redirect has nothing listening. |
| **(B)** Show the success page with a **manual "Continue" button** — user clicks, then redirect fires. | More deliberate, but adds a click that real users would universally hate (their AI client is asking for it). |

I strongly recommend **(A)**. Real clients close the tab instantly so users never see the message; broken/test clients show the message persistently which is exactly what you want.

Want me to do (A)? Or did you have a different design in mind that I'm missing? (If so, walk me through how you imagine the auth code reaches Claude Code without the browser redirect — there might be a flow I'm not seeing.)

content.text:
The page you land on after the redirect is **Claude Code's local callback server** at `http://localhost:CCCC/callback`. That's Claude Code's process running on your machine, not our infrastructure. **We can't customize what it serves** — that's Claude Code's UI.

Here's the architectural reality:

```
[your browser] ──redirect──> [Claude Code's localhost server]
   onchainchess              http://localhost:53053
   (we control)              (Claude Code controls)
```

After the redirect fires, the browser leaves our domain entirely. Whatever appears on `localhost:53053` is shipped by the Claude Code binary on your machine. Anthropic ships that page, not us — its look, its copy, its styling. We have zero ability to brand or change it.

**What we *can* control is the experience *before* the redirect** — the page on our domain (`/authsuccessful`). Three things we could do there:

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| **(A)** Remove the auto-redirect entirely. User sees your "Authentication Successful — close this tab" page and closes manually. | **Breaks Claude Code.** Its localhost server times out waiting for the callback; the AI client never gets connected. |
| **(B)** Increase the auto-redirect delay (e.g., 3–5 seconds) so the user reads your success message before the browser navigates away. | Works. Compromise: your page is visible briefly, then Claude Code's takes over. |
| **(C)** Show your success message AND a "Continue to Claude Code" button. User clicks it to fire the redirect. | Works. Most explicit; requires one click but the page persists until user is ready. |

If your goal is "make the post-auth UX look cleaner overall," the realistic bound is: **make our half look great, then accept that Claude Code's half is whatever they ship.** Want **(B)** or **(C)** for our half?
